title: Power Rankings, Week 8: Philly Grabs the Odds Lead, Randy Actually Trades, and HULK Survives a Bad Beat at No. 1
dek: A 0.92-point upset, a 42-point beatdown and a three-team trade bonanza reshuffle the middle of the Buckaroo Football League with six weeks left.
body: Week 8 had a little of everything. No Banner only HULK put up 128.56 points and lost to Dawgs by 0.92, the kind of result that makes you want to throw the phone across the room. Team Pillbert flattened The Horse is Hea 115.5 to 73.5, and Luffy reacted by handing Philly the league's best title odds at 31%. And in the bottom half, Counting or not Counting GV dropped the week's highest score, 138.28, and sent The fumblers to a fifth straight loss and a playoff chance that cratered from 38% to 5%.

Then there's the trade market, which Kai turned into a personal storefront. He took James Cook III and Jameson Williams from Sonny for Christian Watson and Ashton Jeanty, then immediately flipped Williams, plus Tee Higgins, to Randy for Jonathan Taylor and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Yes, Randy. Made a trade. With another human being. Mark the calendar, because the two trade partners meet head-to-head this week with real stakes on both sides.

power_rankings.blurb: Brucie's crew scored 128.56, got 26.9 from D'Andre Swift, and still lost by 0.92 to Dawgs, which is about as unlucky as fantasy football gets. Nothing is broken here: HULK leads the league with 1,055.9 points, more than 120 clear of anyone else, and still sits at 98% to make the playoffs. Luffy did trim the title odds from 29% to 20%, but one coin-flip loss doesn't cost the throne. Next up is Ghostu-Spider SZN, and a win pushes the playoff odds to 99%.

Philly beat The Horse is Hea by 42, with Jahmyr Gibbs leading the way with 23.8, and climbs from No. 3 to No. 2. At 6-2 with the league's second-best scoring total (933.3), Team Pillbert now owns Luffy's top title odds at 31%, up from 20%. HULK still has the better roster on paper, which is the only reason Alan isn't No. 1. Beat Habibsters this week and the playoff odds hit 100%, which is exactly how he'll tell everyone about it.

Sonny's 73.5 was the lowest score of the week by nearly 28 points, and only Bucky Irving (21) really showed up in the blowout loss to Philly. That drops The Horse from No. 2 to No. 3, and the title odds slid from 24% to 20%. The good news: a 5-3 record and the third-most points keep the playoff odds at 91%. The new pieces from the Kai deal, Christian Watson and Ashton Jeanty, need to look like an upgrade against Counting or not Counting GV, a team that just scored 138.

Three straight wins for Habib, who handled Ghostu-Spider SZN 120.96 to 101.62 behind 22.46 from Drake Maye. At 4-4 the record still looks middling, but the 918.7 points rank fourth, and this team is finally scoring like the two-time champ it is. Holding steady at No. 4, with a big swing coming: beat Team Pillbert and the playoff odds jump to 68%, lose and they fall to 44%.

Kai stole one from the top team in the league, 129.48 to 128.56, with Ja'Marr Chase putting up 25.6, then spent the week rebuilding the roster through two trades that brought in James Cook III, Jonathan Taylor and Amon-Ra St. Brown. That's a lot of firepower for a 3-5 team, and Luffy noticed: playoff odds more than doubled from 19% to 45%, and the title odds went from 5% to 13%. Up one spot to No. 5, and arguably the most dangerous team in the bottom half. Next up is Randy, the guy who just took Jameson Williams and Tee Higgins off his hands.

Five straight losses, the latest a 138.28 to 106.3 defeat to Counting or not Counting GV in which Jaylen Warren (20.8) was the top scorer. The fumblers rank last in the league with 858.7 points, sorry, sixth, which is still not where you want to be, and the playoff odds collapsed from 38% to 5%. Down one spot from No. 5. Randy finally pulled the trigger on a trade for Tee Higgins and Jameson Williams, and a win over Dawgs gets him back to 30%; a loss drops him to 4%.

Zoey's team lost to Habibsters 120.96 to 101.62, with Jordan Love leading the way with 21.52, which at least gave the lone Packers fan in the league something to cheer about. At 3-5 with 762 points, seventh in the league, the scoring just hasn't been there week to week, and the playoff odds dipped from 15% to 7%. Staying at No. 7. The schedule doesn't help: HULK is next, but an upset would push Z² back to 15%.

JMoney had the best day of anyone in Week 8: 138.28 points, the league's top score, powered by a 39.48-point eruption from Joe Burrow, and a win that knocked The fumblers further into the hole. The 2-6 record and league-low 760.8 points keep this team at No. 8, with 1% playoff odds, but it was a reminder that this lineup can make noise. Next up is The Horse is Hea, and Jordan would love nothing more than to be the reason Sonny has a two-game skid.
